answer: If I could design my ideal home, it would be a comfortable two-storey house on the edge of a quiet town, balancing modern convenience with a connection to nature. It would not need to be huge or [[extravagant]]; I value comfort and warmth far more than showing off. I picture large windows that let in plenty of natural light, making the whole space feel open and [[airy]], and a wide veranda where the family could sit together in the evenings with tea. Ideally, it would be somewhere near Sirajganj, perhaps within sight of the Jamuna, so that I could stay close to my parents and grandparents. As for features, a small garden would be essential, somewhere I could grow a few vegetables, plant a mango tree and relax outdoors. Inside, I would want a cosy reading corner with shelves full of books and a proper kitchen, since those are the rooms where I spend most of my time. A spare bedroom would also be important, so that my elder sister and her children could stay whenever they visit from Dhaka. The house would need to be built [[with the monsoon in mind]], raised slightly off the ground so that it never floods. What matters most to me is that it feels genuinely [[welcoming]], both to family and to guests. I would also love it to be in a peaceful area with clean air and friendly neighbours. Honestly, my idea of an ideal home is less about luxury and more about creating a [[sanctuary]] where I can truly relax and feel at peace.

followUps.q: Is your current home similar to your ideal home?
followUps.answer: In some ways. Our flat is comfortable and in a quiet area, but it has no garden and not much natural light. The biggest similarity is that it is full of family, which matters most.

followUps.q: Would you prefer to live in a house or a flat?
followUps.answer: A house, ideally, because of the space and the possibility of having a garden. Flats are more practical and secure in towns, though, so for now I am perfectly happy where I am.

note: Added location near Sirajganj and family, veranda, spare room for his sister's family, flood-proofing; plain 'heart' mark removed, marked 'extravagant' and added 'with the monsoon in mind'.
